newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast prods ease amid light trade.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast prods ease amid light trade.

text.p: U.S. West Coast unleaded gasoline and diesel prices eased Friday, as light trade left the market open to downward pressure from futures markets, traders said.

"Everything's lower because the Merc is down," a broker said, noting March heating oil dropped 0.92 cents a gallon amid light demand. March gasoline, meanwhile, fell 2.24 cents as the product's peak demand season remained months away.
Last week's 612,000-barrel increase in regional gasoline also weighed the market, leaving inventories well-above last year's levels.
Trade faded Friday, as traders attended an industry conference in Utah.
CARB gasoline in Los Angeles fell one cent to 76.50/77.50 cents a gallon, with premium grade holding a four cent advantage.
Los Angeles CARB diesel dipped 1.50 cents a gallon to 82/84 cents, with low sulphur diesel 2.50 cents weaker at 74/75 cents.
Traders said they expected U.S. West Coast products prices to follow the New York futures market this week amid a lack of fundamentals in the region.
